title: Common problems of forages in a cut-and-carry system & Fertilizer application
text:
High sowing rate = weak seedlings
Good sowing rate = strong seedlings

Common problems of forages in a cut-and-carry system:
- A major management problem of forages in the field is nutrient decline.

Leaf comparison of forages from nutrient declined field (left) and a fertile field (right).

Fertilizer application:
- 60-80 % of the nutrients an animal eats are returned in manure and urine.
- Manure is an excellent resource for overcoming nutrient depletion problems.

Dairysquare - Dairy Farming Module Page 31

facts: A high sowing rate results in weak seedlings.
A good sowing rate produces strong seedlings.
A major management problem of forages in the field under a cut-and-carry system is nutrient decline.
Forage leaves from a nutrient-declined field appear pale/yellowish compared to the dark green leaves from a fertile field.
Between 60% and 80% of the nutrients consumed by an animal are returned in manure and urine.
Manure is an excellent resource for overcoming nutrient depletion problems in forage fields.

questions.question: What is the consequence of having a high sowing rate for forage plants?

options.C: Increased leaf surface area and thicker stems
